title: Stellar Flares and Superflares: Flare-Energy, Loop and Ejection-Association Budgets Against Published Event Values

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Settle in.
paragraphs: Welcome in. I am Professor Magnus Andersson, and this is Stellar Flares and Superflares: Flare-Energy, Loop and Ejection-Association Budgets Against Published Event Values. This is lesson 1 of 1 in the full thirty-minute build of this class. In this lesson we take the class's own material in order — nothing here is imported, and nothing is asked later that is not taught here first. We begin here: Settle in.

Settle in. I am Professor Magnus Andersson, and this is Stellar Flares and Superflares: Flare-Energy, Loop and Ejection-Association Budgets Against Published Event Values. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

'Arcade Cooling After the Bastille Day Flare of 14 July 2000: Loop Lengths, Densities and the Two-Stage Decay'. Its stated result: Headline result: early loop conductive s = 10.42; early loop radiative s = 4143; early combined s = 10.4; late loop conductive s = 1334; late loop radiative s = 1381; late combined s = 678.6 Operating principle: in a growing post-eruption arcade the cooling time lengthens with loop length and falls with density, so the observed two-stage decay, fast while the loops are short and hot, slow once they are long and cool,
Now we go one step further into the material.

'Energy Storage for the Great Flare of AD Leonis, 12 April 1985: Starspot Area, Field Strength and the Magnetic Reservoir'. Its stated result: Headline result: radiated energy erg = 1e+34; area at 2kG cm2 = 1.58e+19; area at 3kG cm2 = 9.204e+18; area at 4kG cm2 = 6.272e+18; fraction at 3kG of surface = 0.0008709; stellar surface area cm2 = 1.057e+22 Operating principle: a flare cannot radiate more energy than its magnetic reservoir stores, and the reservoir of an active region scales as the field energy density times a volume set by the spot area, so a meas
The next piece is where this starts to come together.

'Flare Versus Ejection on 28 October 2003: The Kinetic Energy Budget of the Halloween Halo CME'. Its stated result: Headline result: cme mass g = 1.2e+16; cme speed km s = 2459; kinetic energy erg = 3.628e+32; flare radiated energy erg = 4.3e+32; ratio kinetic to radiated = 0.8437; projection corrected speed km s = 2893 Operating principle: an ejection's kinetic energy follows from its mass and speed alone, and setting that energy beside the flare's radiated energy from the same event measures how the released magnetic energy was
Listen carefully here — this piece carries weight in the questions later.

'Loop Cooling in the X2.2 Flare of 15 February 2011: Conductive and Radiative Times Against the Observed Decay'. Its stated result: Headline result: loop density cm3 = 10000000000; loop half length cm = 3000000000; loop temperature K = 12000000; conductive cooling time s = 74.75; radiative cooling time s = 2486; combined cooling time s = 72.57 Operating principle: a hot flare loop cools by thermal conduction to the chromosphere and by radiation, with the conductive time falling steeply as temperature rises and the radiative time taking over as th
We take the pieces in order, because each one stands on the last.

'Loop Length From Decay: The 2016 Superflare on Proxima Centauri and the Reale Scaling Law'. Its stated result: Headline result: decay time s = 400; peak temperature K = 20000000; heating factor F = 1.5; loop half length cm = 3.223e+09; loop half length 1e9cm = 3.223; stellar radius cm = 10700000000 Operating principle: for a freely cooling flare loop the decay time and peak temperature together determine the loop length through the thermodynamic scaling law calibrated on solar and stellar flares, provided the decay is not sus
Stay with me, because the next piece builds directly on that one.

'Loop-Top Density in the X4.8 Flare of 23 July 2002: Emission Measure, Source Volume and the Thermal Energy Content'. Its stated result: Headline result: emission measure cm3 = 2e+49; source volume cm3 = 3.217e+27; loop top density cm3 = 7.885e+10; temperature K = 25000000; thermal energy erg = 2.627e+30; published nonthermal energy erg = 1e+32 Operating principle: a thermal source's emission measure and its imaged volume together fix its density, and the density with the temperature and volume fixes the thermal energy content, which can then be set a
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

Now my worked example — this class's set problem, worked in full. The problem: Take the paper “Arcade Cooling After the Bastille Day Flare of 14 July 2000: Loop Lengths, Densities and the Two-Stage Decay”. Its stated result is: Headline result: early loop conductive s = 10.42; early loop radiative s = 4143; early combined s = 10.4; late loop conductive s = 1334; late loop radiative s = 1381; late combined s = 678.6 Operating principle: in a growing post-eruption arcade the cooling time lengthens with loop length and falls (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong. The worked answer: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

Let us gather what this lesson taught, in order: Settle in; 'Arcade Cooling After the Bastille Day Flare of 14 July 2000: Loop Lengths, Densities and the Two-Stage Decay'; 'Energy Storage for the Great Flare of AD Leonis, 12 April 1985: Starspot Area, Field Strength and the Magnetic Reservoir'; 'Flare Versus Ejection on 28 October 2003: The Kinetic Energy Budget of the Halloween Halo CME'; 'Loop Cooling in the X2.2 Flare of 15 February 2011: Conductive and Radiative Times Against the Observed Decay'; 'Loop Length From Decay: The 2016 Superflare on Proxima Centauri and the Reale Scaling Law'. Those are the pieces — hold them in that order, because the questions follow the same road.

That is the lesson, whole. Below it are the questions — every one of them drawn from what was just taught, and nothing else. The full text of this lesson stays open beside the questions, and going back to read a piece again is learning, not cheating. When you are ready, begin.

questions.teach: Think back to the lesson — the paper 'Arcade Cooling After the Bastille Day Flare of 14 July 2000: Loop Lengths, Densities and the Two-Stage Decay'. The result it reported gives a value for early loop conductive s, and that value is what this question asks for.
questions.teach2: Here is the exact passage from the lesson again: 'Arcade Cooling After the Bastille Day Flare of 14 July 2000: Loop Lengths, Densities and the Two-Stage Decay'. Its stated result: Headline result: early loop conductive s = 10.42; early loop radiative s = 4143; early combined s = 10.4; late loop conductive s = 1334; late loop radiative s = 1381; late combined s = 678.6 Operating principle: in a growing post-eruption arcade the cooling time lengthens with loop length and falls with density, so the observed two-stage decay, fast while the loops are short and hot, slow once they are long and cool, And here is that same result with the words stripped away — just the quantities standing in a row: early loop conductive s = 10.42; early loop radiative s = 4143; early combined s = 10.4. Find early loop conductive s in that row; the value beside it is the one this question asks for. Say it in figures, any honest form: as printed, rounded, or written out in full.
questions.walk: Walk it through with me, step by step. (1) In the lesson, the paper 'Arcade Cooling After the Bastille Day Flare of 14 July 2000: Loop Lengths, Densities and the Two-Stage Decay' stated its result. (2) That result pairs names with values: early loop conductive s = 10.42; early loop radiative s = 4143; early combined s = 10.4. (3) This question asks for the value paired with early loop conductive s. (4) In that row, early loop conductive s stands beside 10.42 — so the answer the lesson gives is 10.42. Now it is yours: say that value, in any honest form.
questions.q: In the lesson, the paper 'Arcade Cooling After the Bastille Day Flare of 14 July 2000: Loop Lengths, Densities and the Two-Stage Decay' reported a number for early loop conductive s. What number did it report?
questions.why: You are doing this because a number you can produce from memory — and defend — is worth ten you have only seen glide past.
